test.name: System of Particles and Rotational Motion - Test 1

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

qns_content.text: A \( 5 \, \text{kg} \) object moves with a velocity of \( -3 \, \hat{\mathbf{i}} + 6 \, \hat{\mathbf{j}} \, \text{m/s} \). What is the magnitude of the velocity of its center of mass?

text_solutions:
For a single object, the center of mass velocity equals the object’s velocity.

Magnitude = \( \sqrt{(-3)^2 + (6)^2} = \sqrt{9 + 36} = \sqrt{45} \approx 6.71 \, \text{m/s} \).

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

qns_content.text: What is the primary difference between translational and rotational motion of a rigid body?

options.text: Translational motion involves rotation about an axis
Rotational motion involves all particles moving with the same linear velocity
Translational motion involves all particles moving with the same velocity, while rotational motion involves the same angular velocity

text_solutions: In translational motion, all particles move with the same linear velocity, while in rotational motion, particles move in circular paths with the same angular velocity about a fixed axis.

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

qns_content.text: What does torque represent in rotational motion?

options.text: The linear force applied to a body
The rotational effect of a force about an axis

text_solutions: Torque is the rotational equivalent of force, causing angular acceleration. It’s defined as \( \mathbf{\tau} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{F} \), with magnitude \( r F \sin \theta \).

qns_content.text: Why is the vector product of two parallel vectors zero?

options.text: Because the angle between them is zero or 180°

text_solutions: The vector product \( \mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b} = ab \sin \theta \) is zero for parallel vectors because \( \theta = 0^\circ \) or \( 180^\circ \), making \( \sin \theta = 0 \).

qns_content.text: In pure rotational motion about a fixed axis, what is true about the motion of particles in a rigid body?

options.text: All particles move in circles with centers on the axis
Only particles on the axis move in circles

text_solutions: In pure rotational motion about a fixed axis, every particle moves in a circular path in a plane perpendicular to the axis, with the center of the circle on the axis.

qns_content.text: In rotational kinematics, what is the rotational analogue of linear acceleration?

text_solutions: Angular acceleration (\( \alpha \)) is the rotational analogue of linear acceleration, representing the rate of change of angular velocity (\( \alpha = \frac{d\omega}{dt} \)).

qns_content.text: What is the unit of torque in the SI system?

text_solutions: Torque is the product of force (N) and distance (m), so its SI unit is Newton-meter (Nm).

qns_content.text: A uniform rectangular lamina of dimensions \( 2 \, \text{m} \times 4 \, \text{m} \) and mass \( 10 \, \text{kg} \) has one corner at the origin along the x- and y-axes. What is the position of its center of mass?

text_solutions:
For a uniform rectangle, the center of mass is at the centroid.

Vertices: \( (0, 0), (2, 0), (0, 4), (2, 4) \).

CM: \( X = \frac{0 + 2}{2} = 1 \), \( Y = \frac{0 + 4}{2} = 2 \). Position: \( (1, 2) \, \text{m} \).

qns_content.text: What happens to the angular momentum of a rigid body if its moment of inertia increases while no external torque acts?

text_solutions: If no external torque acts (\( \mathbf{\tau} = 0 \)), angular momentum (\( \mathbf{L} = I \mathbf{\omega} \)) is conserved. If \( I \) increases, \( \omega \) must decrease to keep \( L \) constant.

text_solutions: Torque (\( \tau = r F \sin \theta \)) depends on the perpendicular component of force (\( F \sin \theta \)), as only this component causes rotation about the pivot, not the radial component.

text_solutions: Moment of inertia measures a body’s resistance to angular acceleration, analogous to mass in linear motion, and depends on mass distribution.

qns_content.text: For a rigid body to be in rotational equilibrium, what condition must be satisfied?

options.text: The moment of inertia must be zero

text_solutions: For rotational equilibrium, the net torque about any point must be zero (\( \sum \mathbf{\tau} = 0 \)), meaning no angular acceleration occurs.

qns_content.text: What is the significance of the right-hand rule in determining the direction of a vector product?

options.text: It determines the magnitude of the vector
It ensures the vector lies in the plane of the two vectors
It defines the direction perpendicular to the plane of the vectors
It calculates the angle between the vectors

text_solutions: The right-hand rule provides a consistent method to determine the direction of the resulting vector (e.g., \( \mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b} \)), ensuring it is perpendicular to the plane of the two vectors in a direction based on their relative orientation.
